title: Sell Mineral Rights in Orangeville, UT
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Orangeville, UT | Emery County
metaDescription: Own coal or coalbed methane minerals near Orangeville, UT? We buy Emery County Ferron Sandstone interests with a straightforward, no-pressure cash offer.
heroLead: Orangeville sits above one of the more productive coalbed methane trends in Utah, the Ferron Sandstone, and that's a different animal from the oil interests we handle in the Uinta Basin.
intro: Orangeville is a small Emery County town built on the same coal seams that made Castle Valley a mining center for a century. What's changed over the last few decades is that the Ferron coal itself became a gas target as much as a mining seam, and mineral owners here can hold interests tied to coalbed methane production even on ground that never had an underground mine.

For families who inherited these interests, the paperwork often still refers to coal leases from an older era, which can make it unclear whether a modern gas well actually falls under the same mineral grant. We sort that out before we ever make an offer.

sections.heading: Coal rights versus gas rights on the same tract
paragraphs: Many Emery County deeds separate coal from oil and gas, or reserve coal to a prior owner while conveying everything else. Before we value an Orangeville interest we confirm exactly which substances your deed actually grants, because a coalbed methane well can be produced under an oil and gas lease even where the coal itself was severed decades ago and belongs to someone else entirely.
This is the single most common source of confusion we see in Castle Valley title work, and it's a detail worth getting right before any sale.

sections.heading: The Ferron Sandstone trend
paragraphs: The Ferron coal fairway running through this part of Emery County has produced gas for decades through dewatering wells that pump groundwater off the coal to release methane, a slower and steadier production profile than a typical oil well's decline curve. Royalty checks from Ferron gas tend to be modest per well but can run for many years, which changes how we think about present value compared to a fast-declining Uinta Basin oil well.
Local operators periodically refracture or recomplete older wells rather than drill entirely new ones, so an interest that's been quiet for a stretch isn't necessarily done producing for good.

sections.heading: What we need from you
paragraphs: A recorded deed, division order, or recent check stub showing your Emery County interest, plus the legal description, gets us started. If you're unsure whether your family retained coal, gas, or both, send what you have and we'll research the Emery County recorder's records in Castle Dale ourselves.
We price Ferron interests against their actual production history and remaining reserve life, not against a flat per-acre number pulled from a different play.

faqs.question: My deed says coal rights only. Can you still buy it?
faqs.answer: Yes, if there's an active or historic coal lease or royalty tied to the interest. We evaluate coal, gas, and combined mineral interests separately since they're valued differently.

faqs.question: Why do Ferron gas wells produce for so long compared to oil wells?
faqs.answer: Coalbed methane wells typically decline more gradually than a conventional oil well once dewatering stabilizes, which can extend the productive life of the well and the royalty stream tied to it.

faqs.question: Do I need to find my original coal lease paperwork?
faqs.answer: It helps but isn't required. We can typically locate the recorded lease and any amendments through the Emery County recorder once we have your legal description.
